comparator.name: Pharmacy
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official 2026-2027 programme-specific TER defines a three-year, 180-EC bachelor with two majors. The selected eponymous Major Pharmacy consists of the shared 60-EC first year, a fixed 60-EC second year, 45 EC of compulsory third-year Pharmacy study including a 15-EC Bachelor Research Project, and 15 EC of restricted Pharmacy electives. The formal curriculum therefore contains 165 EC of compulsory study and 15 EC of restricted choice, with no free minor space. The bachelor programme page confirms the programme's integrated scientific and professional identity across chemistry, biology, medicine, drug development and manufacture, drug action and safety, pharmaceutical care, patient communication and pharmaceutical research.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic bachelor Pharmacy. The 2026-2027 TER offers Major Pharmacy and Major Medical Pharmaceutical Sciences. Major Pharmacy is the eponymous route, contains the programme's full compulsory pharmaceutical-care and drug-science sequence, and is the route that directly reflects the target's broad professional and scientific identity. It is therefore selected independently of UCR fit; the alternative MPS major is a research-oriented route with a 30-EC free minor.

exception.reason: The programme's defining academic identity is a cumulative pharmaceutical-science and professional Pharmacy curriculum: pharmaceutical analysis, technology and biopharmacy; receptor and systems pharmacology; pharmacokinetics, pharmacoepidemiology and pharmacotherapy; drug-group study across major organ systems and diseases; medicinal and organic chemistry; bioanalysis and instrumental analysis; compounding and dosage-form knowledge; pharmaceutical microbiology; laboratory practice; patient care and communication; professional formation; and a pharmaceutical research project. UCR provides a useful biomedical foundation and one dedicated Pharmacology course, but no chemistry curriculum and no sustained pharmaceutical analysis, formulation, pharmacokinetics, pharmacoepidemiology, medicinal chemistry, drug-group, compounding, pharmaceutical-care or pharmacy-practice sequence. A 24-course UCR schedule built from adjacent life science, psychology, data and health courses would replace rather than reproduce the target's defining pharmaceutical progression and is therefore not a defensible substantive match.
exception.curriculumContext: The official 2026-2027 TER accounts for exactly 180 EC in the selected Major Pharmacy: 60 EC of compulsory first-year study, 60 EC of compulsory second-year study, 45 EC of compulsory third-year study including a 15-EC Bachelor Research Project, and 15 EC of restricted Pharmacy electives. The route has no free minor space. Its compulsory core integrates molecular and cellular biology, genetics, physiology, pathology, mathematics and statistics with pharmaceutical analysis, drug design and manufacture, biopharmacy, pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, toxicology, pharmacoepidemiology, pharmacotherapy, patient care, professional practice and laboratory research.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including course names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory and HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics provide a coherent biomedical foundation. HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology is the only dedicated pharmacology course; HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease add relevant disease and immune-system study. HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health, HCBPSYC211 Statistics & Experimental Methods, HCBPSYC311 Medical & Health Psychology and HCBPSYC313 Advanced Research Seminar contribute population-health, methods, patient-context and research perspectives. The workbook contains no chemistry course sequence and no dedicated course in pharmaceutical analysis, pharmaceutical technology or dosage forms, biopharmacy, pharmacokinetics, pharmacoepidemiology, pharmacotherapy, medicinal chemistry, organic synthesis, instrumental or bioanalysis, drug compounding, pharmacy organisation, pharmaceutical care or pharmacy practice. The available adjacent courses therefore cannot sustain a defensible 24-course Pharmacy progression.
